_comment: Mutation testing on the MONEY PATHS only, because a test that passes is not evidence.
This package shipped 220 green tests alongside a route that could never have worked, so
the question 'do these tests notice when the code is wrong' is the one worth paying for.
Stryker changes the code deliberately and checks whether any test fails. A surviving
SCOPE IS DELIBERATE AND SMALL. Two things only: the code that decides what was BILLED
(billing-verify.mjs), and the code that decides WHICH CREDENTIAL a leg gets. Everything
that has ever cost real money here was one of those two. Mutating the other 2,700 lines
would cost hours and tell us about a comment renderer.
NEVER ON THE PULL REQUEST PATH. GitHub bills per job with a whole-minute floor, so the
cheap gate stays cheap and this runs weekly (.github/workflows/mutation.yml).
the eval-reviewer credential ranges 79.46). 76 seconds on one machine. `break` is set at
exactly that baseline, fractional part included: a rounded-down 71 would have passed a
score of 71.00, which is a regression the job would have reported as green. Not an
aspiration either — the run fails on a REGRESSION and does not cry wolf about a number we
already know. Raise it when the survivors are killed; the
survivors themselves are the to-do list, and reports/mutation/mutation.json names them.
Run it locally with: npx @stryker-mutator/core@9.6.1 run
